simple.meaning: עֲקַר (ʻăqar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “pluck up by the roots.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 7:8. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֲקַר (H6132) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עֲקַר (ʻăqar) / H6132 is traced through Daniel 7:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6132. aqar [ עֲקַר ] verb denominative Hithpe`el be rooted up ; — Perfect 3plural (masculine ? see K § 23, 2 ) אִתְעֲקַ֫רוּ Kt, feminine plural רָה - Qr, Dan 7:8 . [ עָר ], עריך see ערר .

occurrences.englishText: “I considered the horns, and behold, there came up among them another horn, a little one, before which three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots: and behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking great things.
